title: Ben Shelton Smashes His Way to First US Open Final
summary:
Imagine playing the biggest tennis match of your life in front of thousands of screaming fans. That's exactly what Ben Shelton did on Friday at the US Open.

Shelton, who is 23 years old, beat his friend Frances Tiafoe in an epic semifinal. The match lasted three hours and 17 minutes! Shelton lost the first set 4-6, but he didn't give up. He came roaring back to win the next three sets 6-3, 6-3, 7-5. The crowd inside Arthur Ashe Stadium went wild.

"Frances is like a big brother to me," Shelton said after the match. The two Americans put on an amazing show, hitting dazzling shots that made the fans cheer.

Now Shelton is in his very first Grand Slam final. That's a huge deal. He is the first Black American man to reach the US Open singles final since Arthur Ashe did it in 1972 — more than 50 years ago!

On Sunday, he will face Alexander Zverev. Zverev is really good. He beat Karen Khachanov to get to the final, and he has beaten Shelton all five times they've played before. But Shelton has the whole crowd on his side.

"I'm going to leave it all on the court," Shelton promised. "Let's do this for the USA!"

Shelton also shared something special. His dad lost his mom earlier this year. "Without her, there's no Ben Shelton standing here today," he said. "This one is for her."
why_it_matters: It shows that losing the first set — or the first try at anything — doesn't mean you're out, and that hard work and staying calm can still take you all the way to the top.

background_read: The US Open is one of the four biggest tennis tournaments in the world, called the Grand Slams, and it is played every year in New York City.
The main court there is named after Arthur Ashe (an American tennis champion who was the first Black man to win a US Open singles title, back in the 1960s).
Alexander Zverev (a German tennis star) has beaten Shelton all five times they have played before, so Sunday's final will be a very big test.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ben Shelton, a 23-year-old American tennis player, who beat his friend Frances Tiafoe in the US Open semifinal.
WHAT: Shelton lost the first set 4-6 but came back to win 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 after more than three hours, reaching his first Grand Slam final.
WHERE: At Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York, where the US Open is played, in front of a wild crowd.
WHY: He is the first Black American man in the US Open singles final in more than 50 years, and he wants to win it for his grandmother, who died this year.
